bullets: Drainage is the design decision that has the biggest impact on any trail, with improper drainage leading to erosion and eventual trail failure.
Excavating with too much of a slope is the most common mistake new trail builders make, resulting in long-term structural issues.
Cuts in the bank on slopes are not optional—ignoring them turns a short-term shortcut into a landslide within years.
Soil structure matters more than people realize, and understanding it enables better trail longevity and resilience.
The framework of land management decisions determines the compromises builders must make, and these should be addressed before excavation begins.
Using tools like Spoke & Wrench or Cascadia Alliance within workflow improves progress visibility and prevents redundant rebuilding.
Machine-made trails are not inherently inferior to hand-made ones—this belief has been re-evaluated based on observed outcomes across multiple teams.
Outside of specific systems like RockShox or Spoke & Wrench, failure modes become harder to detect, making early intervention critical.
